Donaghmede (Donaghmede, Kilbarrack, Raheny, Bayside, Sutton/Howth) — Dublin, Ireland

Relatively safer day Average night

In detail

Press coverage of the Donaghmede Local Electoral Area (which spans Donaghmede, Kilbarrack, Raheny, Bayside and Sutton/Howth) shows no evidence of a general daytime safety problem: shopping streets, parks and the coastal areas around Bayside, Sutton and Howth turned up no dated 2023-2026 news reports of muggings, assaults or notable daytime crime patterns. The recurring, documented concern in this area instead centers on the DART rail line and its stations after dark and in evenings, particularly around Kilbarrack and Howth Junction/Donaghmede stations. TheJournal.ie, 98fm and JOE.ie reported that in June 2021 ambulance personnel and Gardaí were attacked by a group of youths at Kilbarrack DART station. Separately, a violent disorder incident at Howth Junction station (covered by the Irish Times and Irish Examiner) resulted in multiple teenagers being arrested after a melee in which a girl fell under a DART carriage; the case concluded in court with a suspended sentence for one of the youths involved. More recently, TheJournal.ie reported in January 2025 that a 15-year-old boy was charged over a Dart station attack following what was described as a 'complex investigation.' A November 2025 Dublin People article quoted Dublin Bay North TD Barry Heneghan describing Northside DART stations (including those serving this LEA) as comparatively 'neglected' versus Southside stations, reflecting ongoing local concern about station safety and anti-social behaviour. Separately, a serious domestic homicide was reported in Raheny in June 2023 (TheJournal.ie, Newstalk, 98fm) — a woman was found dead in a house and a man was later charged with her murder — but this was a domestic-violence case, not indicative of stranger or street danger to visitors or residents generally. Overall, daytime activity in the area shows no particular concern, while evening/night use of the DART stations along this stretch of line carries a documented, if localized and youth-related, pattern of anti-social behaviour and occasional violent incidents. Sources checked: TheJournal.ie (thejournal.ie); 98fm (98fm.com); JOE.ie (joe.ie); The Irish Times (irishtimes.com); Irish Examiner (irishexaminer.com); Newstalk (newstalk.com); Dublin People (dublinpeople.com).
